what_it_does: Bearer-token API auth: the Supabase access token is sent as Authorization: Bearer and validated per request with a GoTrue round trip
mobile_treatment: The app uses the identical model. No cookie session exists, so there is nothing web-specific to replace. The only change is where the token lives: Keychain and Android Keystore via a secure storage adapter passed to supabase-js, not AsyncStorage.

supabase-js defaults to detectSessionInUrl, which is meaningless on native. The app sets flowType 'pkce', detectSessionInUrl false, and a secure storage adapter. Refresh continues in the background; a refresh failure signs the user out rather than leaving a zombie session.

classification: Improved or redesigned for the app
mobile_treatment: Face ID, Touch ID and BiometricPrompt gate access to the already-stored session. It is a local convenience only: it never becomes a server credential and never replaces the access token. Failing biometrics falls back to the passcode, then to sign-in.

what_it_does: Unconfirmed-email, pending, rejected, approved-not-paid and past_due states
mobile_treatment: All five states ship, as native screens rather than a guard wrapper. The approved-not-paid and past_due states are the compliance-sensitive ones: on iOS they explain the state and where it is resolved, with no purchase control and no link. See section 6.7.
store_policy_note: Apple 3.1.1 and 3.1.3: these banners are calls to action today.

what_it_does: Dual-role accounts: two production auth users own both an artist and a venue profile
classification: Improved or redesigned for the app
mobile_treatment: The app models role as a switcher in the account sheet driven by ownRoles, not by user_metadata.user_type. Switching role swaps the tab bar without signing out, which the web cannot do. Separate accounts on the same email still require a sign-out, and the switcher says so.

what_it_does: Role hint in user_metadata.user_type is navigation only; authority is profile ownership and the ADMIN_EMAILS or admin_users predicate
mobile_treatment: Unchanged, and the app must not tighten or loosen it. A device that guesses wrong about a role gets the wrong tabs, never the wrong data, because every route checks ownership itself.

what_it_does: QR attribution chain: scan, signed 24h claim, localStorage, checkout verification, venue revenue share
mobile_treatment: Verified live on 2026-09-06: the redirect mints the va token and the browser stores it. The app replaces localStorage with secure storage under the same key semantics and the same 24h TTL, and passes the token to checkout unchanged. If this breaks, venues are silently paid nothing and nobody finds out.

what_it_does: QR_ATTRIBUTION_ENFORCE will one day refuse bare slugs
mobile_treatment: The app must send the token, never the bare slug, from day one, so enabling enforcement later is a no-op for app traffic.

what_it_does: Flat 15% platform fee, zero during trial and during a referral fee-free window
classification: Kept entirely in the shared backend
mobile_treatment: Server-side, unchanged. The app displays the resolved rate from GET /api/me/subscription rather than computing it.

what_it_does: Stripe Connect Express payouts with a 14-day hold, immediate for collection orders
classification: Kept entirely in the shared backend
mobile_treatment: Unchanged. Onboarding and the Express dashboard open Stripe-hosted pages in an in-app browser.
store_policy_note: Payouts are not a purchase under either store's rules.

what_it_does: Refunds inside a 14-day statutory window, disputes and chargebacks
classification: Kept entirely in the shared backend
mobile_treatment: Unchanged. Both flows get native screens; the policy stays server-side.

what_it_does: cart_sessions is the data of record, keyed by the Stripe session id
mobile_treatment: On the native PaymentIntent path the key becomes the PaymentIntent id. The row is still written before payment and the webhook still books the order from it, never from the client.

what_it_does: Works cap 8/20/50, active placement cap 2/5/unlimited, outreach 7/15/30 per rolling week
classification: Kept entirely in the shared backend
mobile_treatment: Enforced server-side, unchanged. The app renders the number BEFORE it bites (the ADR 0009 principle) on the Works list, the Spaces list and the placement request sheet.
store_policy_note: The 402 copy is compliance-sensitive on iOS: it states the limit without offering a way to buy past it.

what_it_does: 402 responses from works cap, placement cap, walls cap, visualiser quota and outreach cap
mobile_treatment: Handled by a single error interceptor that renders a native sheet. On iOS the sheet names the limit and the plan that lifts it and stops there; it carries no price, no button and no link.
store_policy_note: Apple 3.1.1: today these render an UpgradePrompt with a CTA.

what_it_does: Public projections: toPublicArtist, redactDemandVenue, coarsenCoordinates to 2dp, column-level REVOKE on PII
mobile_treatment: Every new mobile endpoint must apply the same projection. The anon key ships in the app binary, so the column REVOKEs on artist_profiles and venue_profiles remain the last line of defence and must not be relaxed for convenience.

what_it_does: Artwork image protection against long-press save and context menu
mobile_treatment: Long-press save can be disabled on a native image view, and will be. Screenshots cannot be prevented on either platform, and the plan says so plainly rather than implying the app protects artists more than it can.

what_it_does: Sample pill on the 41 seed artists and 21 seed venues
mobile_treatment: Carried into the app, and made more prominent. See the SEED_CATALOG flag row: this is a store-review risk, not just a copy question.
store_policy_note: 4.2.2 and the App Review metadata rules: fictional catalogue content reads as a placeholder app.

mobile_treatment: Carried across unchanged.

what_it_does: Block and report on conversations, moderation queue, appeal
mobile_treatment: Both actions ship in v1 and must be reachable in at most two taps from any message. Apple 1.2 requires a method for filtering objectionable content, a mechanism to report it, the ability to block abusive users, and published contact information.
store_policy_note: Apple 1.2 is a rejection reason, not a nicety. Artworks and profiles have NO report path today; section 11.6 adds one before submission.

what_it_does: A failed request is not an empty list: honest error states everywhere
mobile_treatment: The convention carries over, and matters more on mobile where connections drop mid-scroll. Every list has four states: loading, empty, error with retry, and offline with cached content plus a staleness marker.
The typed client generated from the zod schemas parses this shape once, so no screen re-implements it.

what_it_does: Per-IP rate limiting, Upstash when configured and in-memory otherwise; Upstash is NOT set in production
mobile_treatment: Per-IP is actively wrong for mobile: carrier-grade NAT puts thousands of users behind one address, so one busy user rate-limits a city. Authenticated routes move to a per-user key and anonymous routes keep per-IP with a per-device-attestation fallback (WP-C-RATELIMIT). Upstash must be configured before launch or none of it is durable.

what_it_does: Cloudflare Turnstile on signup (secret NOT set in production)
mobile_treatment: App Attest (iOS) and Play Integrity (Android) replace it, verified server-side by a new POST /api/auth/attest that fails closed exactly as the Turnstile route does.

what_it_does: NEXT_PUBLIC_FLAG_* flags inlined at build time; flipping one is a redeploy
mobile_treatment: A shipped binary cannot be redeployed. WP-N-CONFIG adds GET /api/app/config returning flags, a minimum supported version, a maintenance flag and per-feature kill switches, cached with a 5-minute TTL and a bundled fallback so a config outage never bricks the app.

what_it_does: Minimum supported version and forced update
mobile_treatment: GET /api/app/config returns minSupportedBuild per platform. Below it, the app shows a blocking update screen with a store link. Above it but below latest, a dismissible prompt.
store_policy_note: Both stores permit a forced-update gate; neither permits blocking the app for any other reason.

mobile_treatment: Every app request sends X-Wallplace-Client: ios|android and X-Wallplace-Build. Response shapes are additive-only for 90 days after a build stops being supported; a removal needs a minSupportedBuild bump first. The contract tests in section 13.3 are what hold this.

what_it_does: Universal links and App Links from every email, QR label and Stripe return
web_location: 102 distinct ${SITE} paths across src/emails and src/app/api
mobile_treatment: apple-app-site-association and assetlinks.json are served from the Next app at /.well-known/, so the domain that already sends the emails is the domain that opens the app. Query parameters are preserved verbatim, and every destination is validated with the same safeRedirect the web uses. Full inventory in appendix B.
A universal link that finds no app opens the web page, which already works. No interstitial, no smart banner on the link itself.
store_policy_note: Apple rejects apps that block content behind an install prompt.

mobile_treatment: Cached: browse feed page 1, saved items, own portfolio, conversation list and the last 50 messages per open thread, own placements. Queued: message sends, artwork image uploads, placement photo uploads. Never offline: checkout, subscription state, payouts, any 402 decision. Conflict rule from src/lib/current-artist-cache.ts: a confirmed write clears the cache, and a cached read is always marked with its age.

what_it_does: Client-side resize to 2000px WebP, 10MB cap, upload straight to public Supabase buckets with owner insert policies
mobile_treatment: Same caps, same buckets, same policies. Native adds HEIC transcoding, EXIF orientation correction and metadata stripping (which the browser canvas path gets for free and a native encoder does not), plus background upload with resumable retry.

Next Image is web-only. The app cannot use it, and Supabase image transformations need a paid plan. Section 12.4 recommends generating three variants (thumb 400, card 800, detail 1600) at upload time with the sharp pipeline that already exists, stored beside the original, plus an on-device disk cache. This is the single largest data-volume decision in the app.

what_it_does: Browse near me, spaces near me, remembered postcode and coordinates
mobile_treatment: Core Location and the Android location APIs with when-in-use permission, primed at the moment the user taps Near me rather than at launch. The 2dp coarsening of published coordinates is server-side and must not be weakened to make the app's distance filter feel sharper.
store_policy_note: Both stores require a purpose string that says what the location is for.

what_it_does: First-party analytics_events with a daily-rotating hashed visitor id from IP and user agent
mobile_treatment: There is no meaningful IP or user agent to hash in an app. The app sends a daily-rotating install identifier it derives locally, never the IDFA or the Android advertising id, so ATT is not engaged.
store_policy_note: App Tracking Transparency applies only to tracking across apps and websites owned by other companies. This is first-party and does not trigger it.

what_it_does: No crash reporting or product analytics is installed anywhere today
classification: Improved or redesigned for the app
mobile_treatment: The app ships with crash reporting and release health from day one, because a crash on a stranger's Android device is invisible in a way a Vercel 500 is not. Section 24 names the tooling and the privacy declarations it forces.
store_policy_note: Any SDK added must carry a signed privacy manifest and appear in the Play Data safety form.

what_it_does: 44px minimum tap targets, enforced by an e2e test
mobile_treatment: Carried over, and raised to the platform minima (44pt iOS, 48dp Android). Dynamic Type and font scaling to at least 200%, VoiceOver and TalkBack labels on every control, reduced-motion respect, and the existing contrast tokens.
store_policy_note: Both stores surface accessibility in review; neither rejects on it alone.

what_it_does: Light theme only; six Premium profile themes and label colour themes
mobile_treatment: Recommendation in section 9.6: ship light-only in v1, matching the web, and declare it. A dark mode that inverts an off-white gallery ground would fight the product's whole visual argument, and half-doing it is worse than not doing it. Raised to the owner in section 17.
store_policy_note: Neither store requires dark mode.

mobile_treatment: The palette becomes one generated token module consumed by both the web CSS variables and the app theme, so a colour is defined once. Section 4.7 gives the mechanism.

what_it_does: British English, no dashes as punctuation, programme not program
mobile_treatment: Applies to every string in the app, including store listing copy, push notification bodies and permission purpose strings. A lint rule over the app's string catalogue enforces it the way the web enforces it.

what_it_does: 58 tables, about 20 service-role-only with RLS on and no policy, client grants revoked
mobile_treatment: Unchanged. The device token table added in section 5.4 follows the same five-step pattern, including the known-acceptable.json entry that the nightly advisor job checks.

what_it_does: Migration numbering: production is ahead of every branch
mobile_treatment: Verified 2026-09-06 via list_migrations: production's highest applied is 138_collection_size_tiers, with a duplicate-numbered 136_artist_profile_review_flow and a 137. Local highest file is 138. The first mobile migration claims 139 and every later one re-checks before it is named.

what_it_does: Reviewer accounts with meaningful data for each role
web_location: demo mode was removed 2026-09-02; the seed script is stale
mobile_treatment: Three reviewer accounts (artist approved and subscribed, venue with a live placement, buyer with an order) with a scripted seed that is kept current. This is an owner deliverable with a real lead time, listed in section 18.
store_policy_note: A reviewer who cannot get past a paywall or an approval queue rejects the app.

what_it_does: App Store and Play listing identity: the Stripe account and Vercel project are still named Wallspace
classification: Improved or redesigned for the app
mobile_treatment: The app is Wallplace everywhere. The Stripe account display name and the Vercel project name are cosmetic and can stay, but the Stripe account name appears on card statements, so it should be changed before the first live charge. Owner action.
store_policy_note: A statement descriptor that does not match the app name generates chargebacks.
